title: Apple's Bid to Use Chinese Chipmaker as Leverage Backfires
excerpt: Apple's attempt to use Chinese memory maker CXMT as leverage against Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix has backfired, with the two Korean...
content_html:
Apple's attempt to use Chinese memory maker CXMT as leverage against Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix has backfired, with the two Korean chipmakers ending up with more pricing power rather than less, DigiTimes reports, citing South Korean and Chinese trade press.


This year, Apple has explored CXMT and fellow Chinese chipmaker YMTC as potential DRAM suppliers, and had progressed to testing CXMT's chips as memory shortages pushed up the cost of almost all Apple devices. Apple hoped a credible Chinese alternative would pressure Samsung and SK Hynix into cutting their own prices, a tactic it has used before with OLED suppliers and contract manufacturers.

CXMT is barred from EUV lithography tools under U.S. export controls, so it has to rely on older DUV equipment that, per a cost analysis cited by TechTimes, requires around 30% more wafer starts to produce the same output. That extra cost means matching Samsung and SK Hynix's prices is CXMT's floor, not a discount it's able to offer, so when Apple pushed for a lower LPDDR5X quote, CXMT turned it down and held pricing at or above the Korean suppliers' own rates.

With that threat neutralized, Apple seemingly lost its main point of leverage. Digital Daily reports that Chinese device makers Huawei and Xiaomi have already locked up most of CXMT's output through long-term, high-price contracts, so the company doesn't need Apple's business badly enough to negotiate.

The result is the opposite of what Apple wanted; without a credible cheaper alternative to point to, Samsung and SK Hynix face less pressure to lower their own prices, at the same time they're shifting production toward high-bandwidth memory for AI servers and tightening the broader DRAM supply. The setback comes after Apple's CXMT plans drew pushback, with politicians demanding Apple commit to not buying Chinese memory chips at all.

content_html_zh:
DigiTimes 援引韩国和中国贸易媒体的报道称，苹果试图利用中国内存制造商长鑫存储来对抗三星电子和 SK 海力士，但结果适得其反，这两家韩国芯片制造商最终获得了更多而不是更少的定价权。

今年，苹果已将长鑫存储和中国芯片制造商长江存储视为潜在的 DRAM 供应商，并已开始测试长鑫存储的芯片，因为内存短缺推高了几乎所有苹果设备的成本。 苹果希望可靠的中国替代方案能够迫使三星和 SK 海力士降低自己的价格，这是它之前对 OLED 供应商和合约制造商使用过的策略。

根据美国出口管制，长鑫存储被禁止使用 EUV 光刻工具，因此它必须依赖较旧的 DUV 设备，根据 TechTimes 引用的成本分析，需要多出约 30% 的晶圆才能生产相同的产量。 这一额外成本意味着长鑫存储的价格与三星和 SK 海力士的价格相当，而不是其能够提供的折扣，因此当苹果要求降低 LPDDR5X 报价时，长鑫存储拒绝了，并将定价维持在等于或高于韩国供应商自己的价格。

随着这一威胁的消除，苹果似乎失去了主要的筹码。 据《数字日报》报道，中国设备制造商华为和小米已经通过长期、高价合同锁定了长鑫存储的大部分产量，因此该公司并不急需苹果的业务来进行谈判。

结果与苹果想要的相反。由于没有可靠的更便宜的替代品可供参考，三星和 SK 海力士面临的降低价格的压力较小，同时他们正在将生产转向人工智能服务器的高带宽内存，并收紧更广泛的 DRAM 供应。 此次挫折是在苹果的 CXMT 计划遭到抵制之后发生的，政界人士要求苹果承诺完全不购买中国存储芯片。
